ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:

As per ISM Code-6.5, The Company should establish and maintain procedures for identifying any training that may be required in support of the SMS and ensure that such training is provided for all personnel concerned.
Evidence:
Port State Control Inspection was carried out by Australia Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) on 18 June 2025 at Sydney, NSW, Australia and the following deficiencies were raised. Vessel was detained for item no. 1 & 2
Note: The item number corresponds to the number as per the AMSA PSC report:
Item-1, No flow through oil content monitor while system in overboard discharge mode. Also, isolation valve on oil content monitor discharge not in accordance with system drawings. Code-30
Corrective Action taken:
Oily Water Separator was tested on board. 15 PPM alarms and three-way valve operation found satisfactory.  The vessel crew has since opened the sampling line and cleared the blockage. It was verified the flow of effluent sample from the 15ppm bilge separator with adequate pressure and flow. Sampling pipe was removed, alarm was activated if no flow.
Nature:
The vessel did not follow the procedures as stated in the ISM code in relation to the OWS operation.

ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:
As per ISM Code-10.2, In meeting the maintenance requirements the Company should ensure that inspections are held at appropriate intervals, any nonconformity is reported with its possible cause and appropriate corrective action is taken.
Evidence: 
Port State Control Inspection was carried out by Australia Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) on 18 June 2025 at Sydney, NSW, Australia and the following deficiencies were raised. Vessel was detained for item no. 1 & 2
Note: The item number corresponds to the number as per the AMSA PSC report:
Item-2, Weathertight cargo hatches not provided with sealing or other arrangements to prevent water from penetrating the ship. Code-30
Corrective Action taken:
Cargo hatches were found as per approved drawing. It was also reviewed by ABS Engineering office that Load Line Condition Assignment
Report (LL-11-D), the imaginary freeboard deck of the subject vessel is 17.3m from BL, which corresponds to the location 3 standard
superstructure heights below upper deck (17.3m=24.2m-3x2.3m), therefore non-weathertight hatch covers are acceptable as per IACS UI
This item was removed from AMSA deficiency list. 
Item-3, Port lifeboat battery cables not secured to battery terminals. Code-17
Corrective Action taken:
The battery terminal for one of the terminals found to be loose and was promptly tightened. The lifeboat engine was then tested using both sets of batteries, and the results were satisfactory.
Item-4, Exposed hot surfaces on emergency generator turbo charger. Code-17
Corrective Action taken:
The thermal lagging on the emergency generator's turbocharger was found to be loose; it was secured and re-fitted to ensure proper insulation and functionality.
Item-5, Earth fault monitors for 440V emergency switchboard turned off. Code-17
Corrective Action taken:
It was 110 V emergency switchboard. Previously it was set to 0.01M ohm. New setting 1 M ohm. Operationally tested and found satisfactory.
Nature: 
Inspections were not held as per the ISM code requirements and company maintenance procedure.

ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:
The Company should ensure that all personnel involved in the Company’s SMS have an adequate understanding of relevant rules, regulations, codes and guidelines.
Evidence:
The ship carried out drills at 1300-1730 on 21 March 2025, 1300-1700 on 21 April 2025, and 0800-1200 on 24 May 2025.
However, the following crew's record of resting hours did not match the drill schedule.
1. One (1) AB failed to record the drill from 1600-1730 on 21 March 2025 and 0800-0830 on 24 May 2025.
2. One (1) deck officer failed to record the drill from 1300-1330 on 21 April 2025 and 1000-1200 on 24 May 2025.
Nature:

Based on the objective evidence gathered it was evident that crew member failed to comply with Hours of Rest Criteria as per STCW 95 code.

ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:
Section 7 of ISM Code:
The Company should establish procedures, plans and instructions, including checklists as appropriate, for key shipboard operations concerning the safety of the personnel, ship and protection of the environment. The various tasks should be defined and assigned to qualified personnel.
Evidence:
The ship prepared Check Lists for Oil Transfer Operation - Bunkering Operation (EP-03-04-03). However, objective evidence indicated that the checklist was not properly recorded, and no markings were made on the ITEMS OF CHECK for the following checklists.

- 
04 June 2025

- 
28 May 2025

- 
20 May 2025

- 
01 April 2025

- 
30 March 2025

Nature: 
The bunkering operation checklists were not properly documented as per the EMC Fleet Bunker Management Manual.

ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:
SE PR-1002 Critical Machinery and Equipment (Rev.12)
Oil Tank High-Level Alarm
2. To verify the function of high-level alarms installed on oil tanks to prevent overfilling, minimize spillage risk and comply with the MARPOL Convention Annex I, Reg. 15. The high-level alarm of oil tanks should be tested at least once every 3 months.
5. The 2/E is responsible to follow the procedures to carry out the test and record the testing result by using the form FM-1002-5 "Critical & essential equipment test record." 
Evidence:
The testing of the Oil Tank High-Level Alarm was not recorded in the FM-1002-5. 
Nature: 
The company procedure was not followed.

ABS Non-Conformity : Requirements: MLC-2006 with amendment 2022, A2.3, Each Member shall require that records of seafarers’ daily hours of work or of their daily hours of rest be maintained.
Evidence: Steering gear failure and emergency steering drill was carried out at 1630-1700 on 02nd January 2025, but rest hour record of 2nd officer were recorded as rest hour.
Nature: MLC-2006 requirement was not compliance.
